# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# Provides a modern, stable base with recent packages for a CPU environment.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required libraries
# - build-essential, cmake, git: Core tools for compiling from source.
# - ca-certificates, wget: For secure network operations.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI for parallel processing, essential for HPC.
# - gfortran: Fortran compiler, a common dependency for scientific software.
# - libfftw3-dev: FFTW library, often used by LAMMPS for performance.
# - libgomp1: GNU OpenMP library, explicitly requested.
# - python3, python3-dev: Python interpreter and headers required by the LAMMPS build system.
# - Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    gfortran \
    libfftw3-dev \
    libgomp1 \
    python3 \
    python3-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a working directory for the source code
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the latest branch of the LAMMPS source code from GitHub
# --depth 1 creates a shallow clone, downloading only the latest commit to save space and time.
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository
WORKDIR /opt/lammps

# Build LAMMPS from source using CMake
# 1. Create a build directory to keep the source tree clean.
# 2. Run cmake to configure the build.
#    - PKG_REAXFF=on: Enables the ReaxFF package as required for 'lammps-reax'.
#    - BUILD_MPI=yes: Compiles LAMMPS with MPI support for parallel execution.
#    - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Specifies an optimized build.
# 3. Run make to compile the code using all available processor cores.
# 4. Copy the compiled 'lmp' executable to /usr/local/bin, which is on the system's PATH.
RUN mkdir build && cd build && \
    cmake ../cmake \
    -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
    -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
    -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp ./lmp /usr/local/bin/

# Set the final working directory for running simulations
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the example input files for the HNS ReaxFF benchmark into the working directory.
# This allows users to immediately run a sample simulation.
RUN cp /opt/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* .

# The container is now ready.
# To run a simulation, use a command like:
# mpirun -np <cores> --allow-run-as-root lmp -in in.hns
